In the late 20th century, [IBM](/wiki/IBM "IBM"), [Microsoft](/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), and [Apple](/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") dominated the worldwide [information technology](/wiki/Information_technology "Information technology") industry.[[17]](#cite_note-17) After the [dot-com bubble](/wiki/Dot-com_bubble "Dot-com bubble") wiped out most of the [Nasdaq Composite](/wiki/Nasdaq_Composite "Nasdaq Composite") [stock market index](/wiki/Stock_market_index "Stock market index"), surviving tech [startups](/wiki/Startup_company "Startup company") expanded their [market share](/wiki/Market_share "Market share") and became dominant in their markets.[[18]](#cite_note-18) The term Big Tech began to appear around 2013, when some economists speculated that a lack of regulation could lead to concentrated [market power](/wiki/Market_power "Market power").[[19]](#cite_note-:2-19) The concept of Big Tech is similar to how the largest oil companies were called [Big Oil](/wiki/Big_Oil "Big Oil") following the [1970s energy crisis](/wiki/1970s_energy_crisis "1970s energy crisis"), and the largest cigarette producers were called [Big Tobacco](/wiki/Big_Tobacco "Big Tobacco"), as [Congress](/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") attempted to regulate those industries.[[15]](#cite_note-BigLabels-15) It is also similar to how, at the beginning of the 21st century, the [mainstream media](/wiki/Mainstream_media "Mainstream media") became dominated by a small number of corporations called [Big Media](/wiki/Concentration_of_media_ownership "Concentration of media ownership") or the media giants.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

The [Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy](/wiki/Larry_O%27Brien_Championship_Trophy "Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy") is awarded annually to the winning team of the [NBA Finals](/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals"), the league's championship series that concludes the playoffs.

The NBA playoffs begin in April after the conclusion of the regular season and [play-in tournament](/wiki/NBA_play-in_tournament "NBA play-in tournament") with the top eight teams in each conference,[[133]](#cite_note-manning270-133) regardless of divisional alignment, competing for the league's championship title, the [Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy](/wiki/Larry_O%27Brien_Championship_Trophy "Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy"). [Seeds](/wiki/Seeding_(sports) "Seeding (sports)") are awarded in strict order of regular season record (with a tiebreaker system used as needed).

Having a higher seed offers several advantages. Since the first seed begins the playoffs playing against the eighth seed, the second seed plays the seventh seed, the third seed plays the sixth seed, and the fourth seed plays the fifth seed, having a higher seed typically means a team faces a weaker opponent in the first round. The team in each series with the better record has home-court advantage, including the First Round.

The league began using its current format, with the top eight teams in each conference advancing regardless of divisional alignment, in the 2015–16 season. Previously, the top three seeds went to the division winners.[[146]](#cite_note-146)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/JFK_and_family_in_Hyannis_Port%2C_04_August_1962.jpg/250px-JFK_and_family_in_Hyannis_Port%2C_04_August_1962.jpg)](/wiki/File:JFK_and_family_in_Hyannis_Port,_04_August_1962.jpg)

The First Family in [Hyannis Port, Massachusetts](/wiki/Hyannis_Port,_Massachusetts "Hyannis Port, Massachusetts"), 1962

Kennedy and his wife were younger than the presidents and first ladies who preceded them, and both were popular in the [media culture](/wiki/Media_culture "Media culture") in ways more common to pop singers and movie stars than politicians, influencing fashion trends and becoming the subjects of photo spreads in popular magazines. Although Eisenhower had allowed presidential press conferences to be filmed for television, Kennedy was the first president to ask for them to be broadcast [live](/wiki/Live_television "Live television") and made good use of the medium.[[423]](#cite_note-american_chronicle-425) In 1961, the [Radio-Television News Directors Association](/wiki/Radio_Television_Digital_News_Association "Radio Television Digital News Association") presented Kennedy with its highest honor, the [Paul White Award](/wiki/Paul_White_Award "Paul White Award"), in recognition of his open relationship with the media.[[424]](#cite_note-426)

The Kennedys invited a range of artists, writers, and intellectuals to White House dinners, raising the profile of the arts in America. On the White House lawn, they established a swimming pool and tree house, while Caroline attended a preschool with 10 other children inside the home.[[425]](#cite_note-427)[[426]](#cite_note-428)

[Vaughn Meader](/wiki/Vaughn_Meader "Vaughn Meader")'s *First Family* comedy album, which parodied the president, the first lady, their family, and the administration, sold about four million copies.[[427]](#cite_note-429)

Golden eagle :: Longevity :: chunk_0024
Golden eagles are fairly long-living birds in natural conditions if they survive their first few years. The survival rate of raptorial birds tends to increase with larger body size, with a 30–50% annual loss of population rate in small falcons/accipiters, a 15–25% loss of population rate in medium-sized hawks (e.g., *Buteo*s or kites) and a 5% or less rate of loss in eagles and vultures. The oldest known wild golden eagle was a bird banded in Sweden which was recovered 32 years later.[[4]](#cite_note-Watson-4) The longest-lived known wild golden eagle in North America was 31 years and 8 months.[[100]](#cite_note-100) The longest-lived known captive golden eagle, a specimen in Europe, survived to 46 years of age.[[101]](#cite_note-Gordon-101) The estimated adult annual survival rate on [the Isle of Skye](/wiki/Skye "Skye") in Scotland is around 97.5%.[[102]](#cite_note-102) When this extrapolated into an estimated lifespan this results in 39+1⁄2 years as the average for adult golden eagles in this area, which is probably far too high an estimate.[[4]](#cite_note-Watson-4)

Survival rates are usually much lower in juvenile eagles than in adult eagles. In the western [Rocky Mountains](/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains"), 50% of golden eagles banded in the nest died by the time they were 2+1⁄2 years and an estimated 75% died by the time they were 5 years old.[[103]](#cite_note-103) Near a wind turbine facility in west-central California, estimated survival rates, based on conventional telemetry of 257 individuals, were 84% for first-year eagles, 79% for 1- to 3-year-olds and adult floaters and 91% for breeders; with no difference in survival rates between sexes.[[67]](#cite_note-Hunt-67) Survival rates may be lower for migrating populations of golden eagles.[[104]](#cite_note-McIntyre2-104) A 19–34% survival rate was estimated for juvenile eagles from [Denali National Park](/wiki/Denali_National_Park "Denali National Park") i

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Loxodonta_africana-cyclotis_skulls_PZSL.png/250px-Loxodonta_africana-cyclotis_skulls_PZSL.png)](/wiki/File:Loxodonta_africana-cyclotis_skulls_PZSL.png)

Skulls of African bush elephant (left) and African forest elephant (right)

The African forest elephant is considerably smaller than the African bush elephant, though the size of the species has been subject to contradictory estimates. A 2000 study suggested that bulls of the species reach a shoulder height of 2.4–3 m (7.9–9.8 ft), and weighed 4–7 t (4.4–7.7 short tons), while cows were about 1.8–2.4 m (5.9–7.9 ft) tall at the shoulder and 2–4 t (2.2–4.4 short tons).[[4]](#cite_note-Grubb_al2000-4) However, a 2003 study of forest elephants at a reserve in Gabon did not find any elephants taller than 2.16 m (7.1 ft).[[12]](#cite_note-12) A 2015 study alternately suggested that fully grown African forest elephant males in optimal condition were only on average 2.2 m (7.2 ft) tall and 2 t (2.2 short tons) in weight, with the largest individuals (representing less than 1 in 100,000 as a proportion of the total population) no bigger than 2.75 m (9.0 ft) tall and 3.5 t (3.9 short tons) in weight.[[13]](#cite_note-probos_mass-13)

The African forest elephant has grey skin, which looks yellow to reddish after [wallowing](/wiki/Wallowing "Wallowing"). It is sparsely covered with black coarse hair, which is 20–200 mm (0.8–8 in) long around the tip of the tail. The length of the tail varies between individuals from half the height of the rump to almost touching ground. It has five toenails on the fore foot and four on the hind foot.[[14]](#cite_note-Turkalo_al2013-14) Its back is nearly straight.[[4]](#cite_note-Grubb_al2000-4) Its oval-shaped ears have small elliptical-shaped tips,[[3]](#cite_note-Matschie1900-3) and the tip of the trunk has two finger-like processes.[[15]](#cite_note-Shoshani1978-15)

[Article II, Section 1, Clause 5](/wiki/Article_Two_of_the_United_States_Constitution#Clause_5:_Qualifications_for_office "Article Two of the United States Constitution") of the Constitution sets three qualifications for holding the presidency. To serve as president, one must:

* be a [natural-born citizen of the United States](/wiki/Natural-born-citizen_clause_(United_States) "Natural-born-citizen clause (United States)");
* be at least 35 years old;
* be a [resident in the United States](/wiki/Residency_(domicile)#United_States "Residency (domicile)") for at least 14 years.[[126]](#cite_note-132)

A person who meets the above qualifications would still be disqualified from holding the office of president under any of the following conditions:

* Under [Article I, Section 3, Clause 7](/wiki/Article_One_of_the_United_States_Constitution#Clause_7:_Judgment_in_cases_of_impeachment;_Punishment_on_conviction "Article One of the United States Constitution"), having been impeached, convicted and disqualified from holding further public office, although there is some legal debate as to whether the disqualification clause also includes the presidential office: the only previous persons disqualified under this clause were three federal judges.[[127]](#cite_note-133)[[128]](#cite_note-134)
* Under [Section 3 of the Fourteenth Amendment](/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution#Participants_in_rebellion "Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution"), no person who swore an oath to support the Constitution, and later rebelled against the United States, is eligible to hold any office. [Argentina](/wiki/Argentina "Argentina") has had many different types of [heads of state](/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"), as well as many different types of government. During [pre-Columbian times](/wiki/Pre-Columbian_Argentina "Pre-Columbian Argentina"), most of the territories that today form Argentina were inhabited by [Amerindian peoples](/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Argentina "Indigenous peoples in Argentina") without any centralized government, with the exception of the [Inca](/wiki/Inca_Empire "Inca Empire") subjects of the [Northwest](/wiki/Argentine_Northwest "Argentine Northwest") and [Cuyo](/wiki/Cuyo_(Argentina) "Cuyo (Argentina)") regions. During the [Spanish colonization of the Americas](/wiki/Spanish_colonization_of_the_Americas "Spanish colonization of the Americas"), the [King of Spain](/wiki/Monarchy_of_Spain "Monarchy of Spain") retained the ultimate authority over the territories conquered in the [New World](/wiki/New_World "New World"), appointing [viceroys](/wiki/Viceroy "Viceroy") for local government. The territories that would later become Argentina were first part of the [Viceroyalty of Peru](/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_Peru "Viceroyalty of Peru") and then the [Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata](/wiki/Viceroyalty_of_the_R%C3%ADo_de_la_Plata "Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata"). The [May Revolution](/wiki/May_Revolution "May Revolution") started the [Argentine War of Independence](/wiki/Argentine_War_of_Independence "Argentine War of Independence") by replacing the viceroy [Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros](/wiki/Baltasar_Hidalgo_de_Cisneros "Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros") with the first national government. It was the [Primera Junta](/wiki/Primera_Junta "Primera Junta"), a [junta](/wiki/Junta_(Peninsular_War) "Junta (Peninsular War)") of several members, which would grow into the [Junta Grande](/wiki/Junta_Grande "Junta Grande") with the incorporation of provincial deputies. This is a list of the best-selling [video games](/wiki/Video_games "Video games") worldwide, ranked up to 50th place by reported [software](/wiki/Software "Software") unit sales. Reliable sources are split as to whether the title of best-selling video game should belong to *[Tetris](/wiki/Tetris "Tetris")*, a 1988 multi-platform [puzzle video game](/wiki/Puzzle_video_game "Puzzle video game") created by [Alexey Pajitnov](/wiki/Alexey_Pajitnov "Alexey Pajitnov"), or to *[Minecraft](/wiki/Minecraft "Minecraft")*, a 2011 multi-platform [sandbox game](/wiki/Sandbox_game "Sandbox game") created by [Markus Persson](/wiki/Markus_Persson "Markus Persson") and developed by [Mojang Studios](/wiki/Mojang_Studios "Mojang Studios"). Some sources consider *Tetris* to be the best-selling video game by combining the sales of all of its different versions, totaling 520 million as of 2022, while others consider the best-selling video game to be *Minecraft*, which has sold 350 million copies as of 2025, rejecting the aggregation of each *Tetris* release.[[a]](#cite_note-Dispute-8) The closest competitor to either is *[Grand Theft Auto V](/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto_V "Grand Theft Auto V")*, which has sold over 225 million copies. The best-selling single-platform game is *[Wii Sports](/wiki/Wii_Sports "Wii Sports")*, with nearly 83 million sales for the [Wii](/wiki/Wii "Wii") console.[[b]](#cite_note-WiiSports-9)

Torres was born on April 15, 1967, to a family in [Los Angeles, California](/wiki/Los_Angeles,_California "Los Angeles, California"), the daughter of [Edward Torres](/wiki/El_Rancho_Hotel_and_Casino#El_Rancho_(1982–92) "El Rancho Hotel and Casino"), and Marylu Kauder.[[2]](#cite_note-downey8162008-2) Her father was a real estate developer and casino owner; her mother Marylu was a former American model.[[2]](#cite_note-downey8162008-2)[[3]](#cite_note-weil6292008-3) Torres grew up in [Beverly Hills, California](/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), the fifth of six children and the older of two girls.[[3]](#cite_note-weil6292008-3) As a seven-year-old, she followed in the footsteps of her older brothers by joining their community [YMCA](/wiki/YMCA "YMCA") for swimming practice; afterward, she signed up for the swimming club in Culver City to train.[[3]](#cite_note-weil6292008-3) At 14, she won the national open championship in the 50-yard freestyle by defeating the then-current champion, [Jill Sterkel](/wiki/Jill_Sterkel "Jill Sterkel"), a college junior.[[4]](#cite_note-levin6181984-4)

She attended the Westlake School for Girls (now [Harvard-Westlake School](/wiki/Harvard-Westlake_School "Harvard-Westlake School")),[[2]](#cite_note-downey8162008-2) and competed for the Westlake swim team under coach Alison Esses from the seventh grade through her sophomore year in high school.[[5]](#cite_note-white3152013-5) She was also a member of the Westlake basketball, gymnastics, and volleyball teams.[[5]](#cite_note-white3152013-5) During her 1983–84 high school junior year, she left home to swim for the [Mission Viejo Nadadores](/wiki/Mission_Viejo_Nadadores "Mission Viejo Nadadores") in [Mission Viejo, California](/wiki/Mission_Viejo,_California "Mission Viejo, California"), while training for her first Olympics under coach [Mark Schubert](/wiki/Mark_Schubert "Mark Schubert").[[4]](#cite_note-levin6181984-4)

**Lai Ching-te** ([Chinese](/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): 賴清德; [pinyin](/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Lài Qīngdé*; born 6 October 1959), also known as **William Lai**, is a Taiwanese politician and physician who has served as the eighth [president of the Republic of China](/wiki/President_of_the_Republic_of_China "President of the Republic of China") since 2024. A member of the [Democratic Progressive Party](/wiki/Democratic_Progressive_Party "Democratic Progressive Party") (DPP), he has been [the party's chairman](/wiki/List_of_leaders_of_the_Democratic_Progressive_Party "List of leaders of the Democratic Progressive Party") since 2023.

Born in [Wanli District, New Taipei](/wiki/Wanli_District,_New_Taipei "Wanli District, New Taipei"), Lai studied medicine at [National Taiwan University](/wiki/National_Taiwan_University "National Taiwan University") and [National Cheng Kung University](/wiki/National_Cheng_Kung_University "National Cheng Kung University"), and earned a master's degree in [public health](/wiki/Public_health "Public health") from [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") in 2003. After practicing [internal medicine](/wiki/Internal_medicine "Internal medicine") as a [chief physician](/wiki/Chief_physician "Chief physician") at two hospitals, he won election in 1996 to represent [Tainan City](/wiki/Tainan_City "Tainan City") in the [National Assembly](/wiki/National_Assembly_(Republic_of_China) "National Assembly (Republic of China)"), then served in the [Legislative Yuan](/wiki/Legislative_Yuan "Legislative Yuan") from 1999 to 2010. He was the first [Mayor of Tainan](/wiki/Mayor_of_Tainan "Mayor of Tainan") from 2010 to 2017 and the 26th [Premier of the Republic of China](/wiki/Premier_of_the_Republic_of_China "Premier of the Republic of China") from 2017 to 2019.
